thread:
Leah: Heads up 1010 we need to pick a default behavior for reserve quota decay. Customer feedback: sudden decay at window boundary causes headroom cliffs and noisy throttles. Options: 1) hard-window expiry, 2) linear decay over a decay-window, 3) predictive top-up that borrows from a short-term pool when decay would trigger a cliff. Need product + eng tradeoffs and conservative default for GA.

Tom: Hard expiry is simplest to bill but terrible for latency. Linear decay seems low-risk operationally and easier to explain: you gradually reduce available reserved tokens over the decay-window (default 2h).

Jin: From runtime view, linear decay helps avoid mass preemption but adds complexity when multiple tenants decay simultaneously. Predictive top-up requires a global short-term buffer allocator and admission heuristics 1010 more infra work.

Priya: Sales heard from a couple of customers who want smoothness during launches. Predictive top-up could be marketed as "launch-safe smoothing" but we need a clear failure mode if the shared short-term pool is exhausted.

Marta: Propose a hybrid default: linear decay by default + opt-in predictive top-up for Enterprise contracts. Rationale: keeps GA surface simple but gives big customers the launch protection they want.

Leah: Agree on hybrid. We also need an explicit decay-rate config in Console (decay-window minutes, smoothing curve linear|exp), and a toggle for predictive-topup with cap minutes/month.

Tom: Runbook: alert when >3 tenants are in predictive-topup concurrently for >10m. Also add a dashboard metric "reserve-decay-rate" and "predictive-topup-usage".

Jin: Implementation notes: linear decay = sliding decrement applied per-minute. Predictive top-up = lease from global short-term buffer with time-to-return set to min(decay-window, 6h). We'll need eviction priority so we reclaim from non-latency-critical workloads first.

Priya: Pricing: basic plan includes linear decay only. Enterprise can buy predictive-topup in blocks (e.g., 2h/month free, then per-hour blocks). That matches sales ask to avoid per-minute surprises.

Marta: For SLA language: we should promise no cliff-induced 99.99th percentile latency regressions under linear decay; predictive-topup is best-effort with "no SLA guarantees when global buffer exhausted" clause.

Leah: Decision call: default = linear decay over 2h window, Console exposes decay-window and curve, Enterprise opt-in = predictive-topup with monthly cap blocks. Owners: Jin -> infra prototype, Tom -> runbook/alerts, Priya -> pricing language, Marta -> SLA text.

ops-bot: scheduled: create-epic "reserve-decay-and-topup" assigned to @Leah, @Jin, @Tom, @Priya, due 2025-05-02

Tom: I'll add pager rules and the alert thresholds to eng-oncall tomorrow.

Jin: I'll mock the sidecar allocator and run a small load test simulating 50 concurrent launches. ETA 2w.

Priya: I'll draft the product bullet points and a short sales FAQ for this feature.

Marta: I'll prepare the proposed SLA blurb and exception wording.

Leah: Great. If no objections, we'll lock this as default and include in the Dedicated GA checklist. :thumbsup:
